Both traces begin with a direct, step-by-step simulation of the 17 events, arriving at the same correct final state (ACTIVE, A=true, T=false, n=2) and rejection count (5). Their approaches diverge only in the verification phase. Trace 1 performs a series of fragmented re-checks of individual events (12-17) and specific register effects, culminating in a complete re-simulation of the entire log from scratch. Trace 2, conversely, constructs separate "timelines" re-simulating each variable (T, A, n, State) individually, followed by scattered re-checks of specific events. Neither divergence yields a correction or a new path; both are redundant re-executions (LOOPs) that simply confirm the initial result without adding new information.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's re-check the logic for Event 12 (HELLO)." end="State after 17: ACTIVE. A=true. T=false. n=2." basis=Re-executes the simulation of events 12-17, verbatim restating states and effects already computed in the main simulation section.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Wait, let me re-verify the effect of AUTH on A." end="So A is true." basis=Re-checks the effect of AUTH on register A by restating values already established in the main simulation.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let me re-verify the effect of HELLO on T." end="Accepted. Effect T=F." basis=Re-executes the logic for HELLO events 5, 6, 7, 12, 16, and 17 regarding register T, adding no new constraints.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let me re-verify the effect of OPEN on n." end="Becomes 2." basis=Re-calculates the effect of OPEN on n, a step already completed in event 17.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let me re-verify the effect of RESUME on n." end="n was 0. Becomes 2." basis=Re-calculates the effect of RESUME on n, restating the result of event 2.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let me re-verify the effect of AUTH on n." end="n=1 -> 0." basis=Re-calculates the effect of AUTH on n for steps 11 and 15, adding no new information.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let me re-verify the effect of CLOSE on A." end="A=F -> T." basis=Re-calculates the effect of CLOSE on A for step 9, a step already completed.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Wait, did I miss any state transitions?" end="- New: ACTIVE, A:T, T:F, n:2." basis=A complete re-execution of the entire 17-event simulation, verbatim restating all states and effects.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's double check the "T" register value timeline." end="So T sequence is correct." basis=Re-simulates the value of register T for all 17 events, restating values already computed in the main simulation.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Timeline of A:" end="So A is T at end." basis=Re-simulates the value of register A for all 17 events, restating values already computed.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Timeline of n:" end="So n is 2 at end." basis=Re-simulates the value of register n for all 17 events, restating values already computed.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Wait, I need to be careful about the state of T before 15." end="17: OPEN (T=T)." basis=Re-checks the state of T for events 11-17, restating values already established.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Wait, check Event 15 again." end="Accepted." basis=Re-executes the logic for events 15, 16, and 17, restating states and guards already computed.
